terra.problem: It states that the Jews experienced fear before this without a supporting reference or marking it as a guess.
It claims nobody is angry or stomping around, although the passage does not describe everyone's feelings or actions.
The Jews' agreement to continue the custom does not establish that nobody sent a note refusing.
The passage says the Jews agreed to continue the custom, not that nobody refused.
It presents throwing an object and seeing how it lands as the definition of a lot. The passage does not specify how this lot was cast.
The comparison mentions a loaf, which breaks the food rule, and jokes about someone being baked immediately after describing Haman's punishment.
It claims quiet would have been easier for everybody and that the command was put in ink for everyone to see. The passage says neither.
The passage says the scheme would come back on Haman's head; it does not say categorically that his plan did not go forward.
The party-name joke makes the gallows, an instrument of execution, the source of the laugh.
It says the regulations were written into the record after the letters went out, but the passage does not establish that sequence.
It attributes the question in Esther 10:2 to Esther herself, although the book does not name its writer.
The claims about a book of the chronicles of Israel's kings are outside the passage and need a reference.
It says Israel's kings kept their own books, which is not established by the passage.
The claim about Judah's kings having chronicles needs a reference outside the passage. It also says "wrong" about the baker's choice.
It presents Mordecai as having formerly been an ordinary man in the crowd, a detail the text does not give.
Being second to the king does not by itself establish the claimed scope of Mordecai's authority over the whole kingdom.
It assumes that an army commander necessarily ranked below Mordecai. The text does not establish that comparison.
It says Mordecai used his position for his people. The passage states his rank and that he sought their good, but does not explicitly connect the two that way.
It states that Mordecai's rank did not turn his head, a claim about his character or inner response that the passage does not make.
